title: Choose the visual world for the Android app
question: The roll assigned Clear Drawers. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Clear Drawers
options.lineage: stacking translucent storage drawers with slip-in labels
options.thesis: Every place is a frosted drawer you can see into, and a path is the stack.
options.viewport: Search bar with mic and scan on top; every item row shows its path as stacked translucent drawer tabs, tinted by room; one Add FAB; Find, Places, History in the nav bar.
options.risk: Translucent tints turn to mush in dark theme unless each room colour is a real tonal role.

raised.raise: One axis rules: the path always reads down a single leading-edge spine, on every screen.
Fixed scale: every drawer tab is the same height and type size everywhere, so paths compare at a glance.
Accent discipline: the deep teal is spent only on the one primary action per screen.
Scale contrast does the hierarchy: item name large, path small, no boxes or rules to separate them.
One thing owns the sheet: an opened item fills its sheet with that item and its actions, nothing else.

options.label: Transit Map
options.thesis: Every room is a coloured line; units and boxes are stops; the item is the terminus.
options.viewport: Search on top; each item row carries a tiny route line from room to item; Places draws each room as a line with its units as stations.
options.risk: The most familiar wayfinding move for paths; long paths need to wrap without breaking the line.

options.label: Boarding Pass
options.thesis: Each item is a pass: its path printed as labelled segments, recent moves held lit like a gate change.
options.viewport: Search on top; rows as passes with ROOM | UNIT | BOX segments; an item moved today keeps an orange edge until you open it.
options.case: Holds clarity (segmented paths, held change-state) but loses identification: it reads as travel, not home.
options.risk: Reads as an airline app if the segments get too literal.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: A vertical centre staff where shape, shading and length carry meaning.
options.viewport: A centre staff with items as shaded blocks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: households do not read notation, and paths are not durations.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject followed through stages on fixed-scale plates.
options.viewport: Five aligned plates on one baseline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a home inventory has no seasons to compare.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: One neutral scale and an accent used four times.
options.viewport: Claim and proof pairs in a strict grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a marketing grammar with no home in it.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the viewport, next one a snap away.
options.viewport: One item per screen with a right action rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: finding a thing is a search, not a scroll of one at a time.
options.kept: One thing owns the screen when it is open.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.viewport: One giant glyph and an axis slider.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in the product is about type.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale contrast, nothing else.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A stock Material 3 utility app, the way Google's own apps are built, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Material search bar, list items with supporting path text, an Add FAB, a three-tab nav bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other utility on the phone, by design.
